scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A winning banner
scenes.caption: During a fictional game demonstration, Meera sees a banner promising a rare costume. It says she has been specially selected. The class pauses the imaginary screen before anybody clicks, because an exciting reward can distract from what comes next.
scenes.dialogue: What does it ask us to do?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Read the request
scenes.caption: The next card requests a school login and a small unlocking payment. Neither is needed to examine the offer. Meera writes two requested actions on her offer-check card, separating the promised costume from the information and money being sought.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: The countdown
scenes.caption: A timer says the reward expires in two minutes, and a note says not to tell adults. These are pressure tactics, not proof that the prize exists. A padlock and copied game logo would not establish who controls the page either.
scenes.dialogue: Urgency is a reason to pause.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose a route
scenes.caption: Meera can pay, ask the banner’s own chat helper, or check with a guardian through the game’s already known official route. Choose a route whose contact details do not come from the suspicious offer.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A recorded result
scenes.caption: She closes the offer and records the request without entering details. Her guardian helps check the known service. The class cannot establish the sender’s identity from the banner alone; avoiding exposure does not require solving that mystery.
scenes.dialogue: Record the action, not a guess.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: A different hook
scenes.caption: Tomorrow’s card offers a free scholarship badge but demands secrecy instead of speed. In the lab, revise the offer-check card and explain why a different reward does not change the need for independent checking.
